entries.text: The older account below describes the pre-replay source audit. Both externally authored JenW1N submissions have since been replayed against the exact reconstructed historical Lean targets: part (i) affirmatively, part (ii) as a counterexample to the proposed existential assertion. The original conventions count unordered representations, permit equal summands, and allow zero in the underlying natural-number set. The replay matched target-type hashes, rejected altered targets and reported only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. It used Lean 4.33.0 with the pinned Mathlib revision. This is historical target-level verification, not a GCL discovery or MATHCERT certification. The original solver retains credit. The earlier statement that both directions still require proof is superseded at this exact historical target scope; broader paper/source correspondence remains separate.
entries.title: Historical formal replay completed

entries.text: The earlier source audit below did not compile the external proof. That replay has since been completed and internally adjudicated: a single positive constant C works for infinitely many natural numbers n, simultaneously for every positive shift k, bounding the number of distinct prime factors of n+k by C times k. The pinned external proof compiled on Lean 4.33.0 with nine recorded compatibility patches and standard axioms only; all seven verification stages passed. This verifies the original distinct-prime omega proposition, not the stronger published multiplicity-counting Omega theorem or the full Tao–Teräväinen paper. The missing author Leanization map and unpatched-source equivalence remain separate obligations. MATHCERT was not submitted; preserve external proof credit.
entries.title: Exact distinct-prime theorem verified

entries.text: The powers-of-two subseries T described below is now formally verified without certification: the protected verification manifest records all seven stages PASS. This supersedes the older proposal to formalize T, but not the open irrationality question for the full totient series S. The newer Cook-phase research (WP09-J/K) establishes a scoped multiplicativity-defect detector and a quantitative complex-modulus separation for long products of genuine Cook phases of certain two-unit perturbations. For the actual totient, the anchored word is identically one. Neither the long-word result nor its finite tests imply the required one-point Cook first-harmonic cancellation or weighted prime-cofactor estimate. Those bridges remain open. No irrationality proof of S or MATHCERT certification is claimed.
entries.title: Auxiliary irrationality result verified; full series open

entries.text: MATHSOLVE has a source-locked extracted-declaration bridge for the original provider statement, and a Lean proof of Bernstein’s lemma for countable families of infinite sets. This is not native integration into the entire upstream provider package. The latest protected route proves that an inclusion-minimal vertex cover gives a two-colouring under the no-singleton-intersection hypothesis; a finite-trace cover yields a minimal subcover. The latter extra hypothesis is not universal: a doubled maximal almost-disjoint family supplies a paper-level obstruction to finite-trace covers, not a counterexample to Property B. Establishing a minimal or suitably witnessed cover under the unrestricted original assumptions remains open. No MATHCERT certification.
entries.title: Protected set-system reductions

entries.text: Protected research develops exact values in restricted star-forest families and lower bounds for arbitrary finite simple host graphs. The fourth source-proved original Ramsey transfer was restored in the recursive certificate procedure. On its declared grid of 179,928 three-blue target profiles, the current trace records 165,741 exact joint-residual certificates and 132,393 exact original Ramsey certificates; 14,187 joint cases remain UNKNOWN by these sufficient rules. The grid counts are not fractions of the unrestricted conjecture proved, and UNKNOWN is not a counterexample. Paper-level claims remain under mathematical review; finite traces are checked. The unrestricted conjecture remains open/partial and has no MATHCERT certification.
entries.title: Restricted size Ramsey theorems and proof certificates

entries.text: GCL reconstructed the published off-diagonal counting argument for finite simple hosts when the smaller bipartite side has size at least two and the larger exceeds it by at least two. Two finite graph enumerators checked 36,168 cases; twelve supporting Lean statements were replayed, with three altered targets rejected. These are not a full Lean proof of the published counting lemma or the diagonal size Ramsey asymptotic. The Mathlib graph-semantics bridge, degree-rank counting injection, analytic sum and probabilistic colour argument remain to be formalized. The diagonal original problem remains open; MATHCERT was not submitted.
entries.title: Qualified off-diagonal proof verification

entries.text: The older legacy account says no mathematical source audit had returned. Protected Phase A source reconciliation and Phase B review now exist, including the general least-common-multiple periodicity lemma: a finite system of congruences covers the integers exactly when it covers every residue modulo their common least multiple. Finite adversarial tests support that bounded result. The original conjecture is classically settled, but these records do not establish independent replay of Hough’s or BBMST’s analytic proofs, a Lean kernel replay, or MATHCERT certification. Phase C is separate. This remains a legacy exemplar, not a newly admitted article.
entries.title: Bounded source and periodicity work recovered

entries.text: The protected frontier records formalized finite reductions, verified finite deletion/tail/residue results and the independently verified dyadic mass bridge. For each fixed progression length k, the reciprocal-divergence question is reduced to convergence of the sum of normalized extremal progression-free densities on dyadic scales; the reverse block construction was also verified. For length four the missing density-dependent decay estimate remains open. The gluing-radius equivalence is a native proof candidate awaiting its specified verification, and the joint-witness incompatibility is a residual attack, not parent theorem closure. Longer progression lengths remain separate. This legacy exemplar has no new editorial admission or MATHCERT certification.
